title: Super funds shrug off higher inflation in August
full_text:
Following a subdued start to the financial year, super funds experienced stronger growth in August with the median balanced option returning 0.8 per cent.
Research house SuperRatings estimated the median balanced option returned 0.8 per cent to members over the month while the median growth option grew by an estimated 1 per cent in August. The median capital stable option is estimated to rise a more modest 0.4 per cent.
This is an improvement from returns of 0.3 per cent for the median balanced option in July.
“Despite persistent inflation and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, the first two months of FY27 have seen super funds deliver a solid start to returns for their members,” said Kirby Rappell, director of SuperRatings.
Balanced: 0.8 per cent for the month, 7.4 per cent over one year, 9.3 per cent per annum over three years, 6.2 per cent per annum over five years, 7.2 per cent per annum over seven years and 7.5 per cent per annum over 10 years.
Growth: 1 per cent for the month, 8.2 per cent over one year, 10.9 per cent per annum over three years, 7.3 per cent per annum over five years, 8.7 per cent per annum over seven years and 8.8 per cent per annum over 10 years.
Capital stable: 0.4 for the month, 4.7 per cent over one year, 6.1 per cent per annum over three years, 4.0 per cent per annum over five years, 4.2 per cent per annum over seven years and 4.5 per cent per annum over 10 years.
It was a similar story in the pensions space, the median balanced pension option increased by an estimated 0.9 per cent, the median capital stable pension option returned 0.4 per cent over the month, while the median growth pension option is estimated to have returned 1 per cent for the same period.
However, the research house warned the next few months could remain unclear as the US-Iran conflict weighs on commodity prices and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) moots further interest rate rises.
Rappell continued: “Super funds have generated pleasing results to members in the opening months of the new financial year. However, moderating consumer demand, ongoing geopolitical instability, the prospect of further rate hikes and continued volatility within the artificial intelligence sector all have the potential to create investment headwinds.”
